The petitioners have filed this claim petition against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Kum.Tejashree.Y D/o Yadukumar.M, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 06.06.2022 at about 12.00 p.m the deceased Tejashree.Y was travelling with her parents and maternal aunt as a copassenger in the vehicle involved in the accident and proceeding to Kukke Subramanya, while travelling so from Kaikamba Cheru,
Bilinele Village, Kadaba Taluk, in between Gundya Subramanya from Gundya Road,
the driver of the Hyundai I20 Car bearing No.KA41MB7975 drove his car in rash and negligent manner, with high speed, lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the bridge wall.

Due to this Tejashree sustained severe head injuries and was immediately taken to Subramanya Primary Health Centre and later taken to Kadaba hospital wherein she declared dead by the doctor on the spot and petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards funeral, obsequies and (SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 transportation of deadbody.
As on the date of accident the deceased was student studying at 10 th Standard in Sri Vijaya Vidya Mandira School at Vasanthapura, Bengaluru.

Due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have undergone irreparable loss and petitioner No.1 fell sick due to mental agony and they have lost love of their daughter and sister and deceased was brilliant student and was very skillfull in the dream of pursuing UPSC exams serving the nation

and if she Yadukumar M vs Ravi Chandra on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9223321/
2 would alive, she would take care of the petitioners in their old age.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of above said offending Car by its driver and the Kadaba Police have registered a case against said driver of the offending Car.
The respondent No.1 being the Driver, respondent No.2 being the insurer and respondent No.3 being the R.C. Owner of the offending Car.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/ with interest and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.2 and 3 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only respondent No.2 has filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and admits that this respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of Nagesha.S in respect of Car bearing No.KA41MB7975 and the liability of this respondent if any, is limited to terms and conditions of the policy, provisions of M.V.
Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of the car, valid RC and FC and further denied age, manner of accident, involvement of the vehicle, expenses incurred by the petitioners.

There was no rash/negligence on the part of the driver of the car and the driver of the car did not have valid driving licence to drive the car at the time of accident and hence there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

The Car bearing No. KA41MB7975 was registered for private vehicle and at the time of accident the vehicle was used for commercial purpose with excess seating capacity, thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and hence this respondent is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and further denied that the petitioners are the legal representatives and dependents on the earnings of the deceased and deceased was student.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant and (SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 excessive.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.
05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 01.

Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Tejashree.Y D/o YaduKumar?
02.

Whether petitioners prove that deceased Tejashree. Y., D/o. Yadukumar., died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 06.06.2022 at about 12.00 p.m., on Kaikamba Cheru, Bilinele Village, Kadaba Taluk, Dakshina Kannada, due to negligent act of driving of the Car bearing registration No. KA41MB7975 by its driver as alleged in the petition?

Yadukumar M vs Ravi Chandra on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9223321/
3
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed their side evidence.

Inspite of sufficient opportunities, the (SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 respondents have not lead evidence, hence,
respondents evidence is taken as nil.

07. Heard the arguments advanced by the counsels for petitioners and respondent No.2 and perused the records.
08.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 :
As per final order  for the following:

REASONS 09. Issue No.1 & 2: In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.

10. The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments. During the course of cross examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that the offending Car bearing (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 No.KA41MB7975 belongs to deceased Nagesh and as on the date of accident in the said car six persons were traveling and deceased Nagesh was the cousin brotherin law of his wife and that one Ravichandra was driving the said car.
In the accident his daughter and Nagesh died.
At the time of accident his daughter was studying at X standard.

On perusal of his evidence, it is very much clear that the respondent No.1 is the driver of the offending car,
respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said car and respondent No.3 is the wife of R.C. Owner deceased Nagesh.
11 . Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 15 documents as Ex.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by Kadaba Police against driver of offending car for his rash and negligent driving.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint given to the Police against driver of offending car for his rash and negligent driving and has caused the accident.

Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Sketch which indicates that the respondent No.1 the driver of the offending car has rashly and negligently driving the car and hit against bridge wall and caused the accident and caused death of deceased Tejashree who is the daughter of the petitioners No.1 and 2 and sister of petitioner No.3 and the owner of the said car by name Nagesh also died.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Spot (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 Mahazar.

Ex.P.5 is Yadukumar M vs Ravi Chandra on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9223321/
4
copy of Post mortem report shows that deceased Tejashree was died in the road traffic accident due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of head injury.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Charge sheet which was filed against driver of offending car for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident and causing death of deceased persons.
Ex.P.7 is copy voluntary statement of accused.
Ex.P.8 is copy of arrest notice.

Ex.P.9 is copy of IMV report shows that as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 who is the driver of the offending car had drove the car in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bridge wall and caused death of deceased and due to said accident the front portion of the car was completely crushed and damaged.
Ex.P.10 is Photographs of the accident spot.
Ex.P.11 is copy of Inquest report of deceased Tejashree who died in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P.12 is copy of Aadhaar card of deceased Tejashree.
Ex.P.13 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.1.

Ex.P.14 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.2 and Ex.P.15 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.3.
12.

On going through the above oral and documentary evidence of petitioners, it clearly goes to show that deceased Tejashree was a daughter of (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 petitioners No.1 and 2 and sister of petitioner No.3 and it is further established and proved that the deceased Tejashree.Y was died in road traffic accident that occurred on 06.06.2022 at about 12.00 p.m at Kaikamba Cheru, Bilinele Village, Kadaba Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of Hyundai I20 Car bearing No.KA41MB7975 by its driver.
Hence, the petitioners have proved Issues No.1 and 2.

Accordingly, this Issues No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Tejashree.Y, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioners in their pleading and evidence has stated that as on the date of alleged accident the deceased was aged about 15 years and was studying in 10th standard and petitioners No.1 and 2 have lost their love and caretaker daughter and petitioner No.3 last her beloved sister and she is a brilliant student and was very skillfull in the dream of pursuing UPSC exams serving the nation and due to untimely death,
the petitioners are put to mental shock and agony and if she would alive, she would take care of the petitioners in their old age.
. The petitioners have not produced any school records or birth certificate of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card of the deceased wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 10.02.2007.
The alleged accident occurred on 06.06.2022.
Even taking into consideration of the said document, the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 15 years.
It is also appears that deceased was a minor as on the date of accident.

15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Kishan Gopal and another V/s Lala and others reported in AIR 2014 SC (SUPP) 173 wherein it is observed that, "Further, the deceased boy, had he been alive would have certainly contributed substantially to the family of the appellants by working hard".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid reasons, it would be just and reasonable for us to take his notional income of Rs.30,000/ and further taking the young age of the parents, namely mother who was about 36 years old, at the time of accident, by applying the legal principle laid down in the case of Yadukumar M vs Ravi Chandra on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9223321/
5 Sarva Verma, the multiplier of 15 can be applied to the multiplicand.

Thus, 30,000 x 15 =
Rs.4,50,000/ and Rs.50,000/ under conventional heads towards loss of love and affection,
(SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 funeral expenses, last rites as held in Kerala State Road Transport Corporation V/s Susane Thomas case, which is referred to in Lata Wadhwa's case and the said amount under the conventional heads is awarded even in relation to the death of children between 10 to 15 years old.

entities.text: Kerala State Road Transport Corporation V/s Susane Thomas
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case also we award Rs.50,000/ under conventional heads.
In our view, for the aforesaid reasons the said amount would be fair, just and reasonable compensation to be awarded in favour of the appellants.

16. In a case Meena Devi V/s Nunuchand Mahto and others, Special Leave Petition No.5345/2019 wherein Apex Court held that, "Applying the ratio of the said Judgments, looking to the age of the child in the present case, i.e., 15 years, the principles laid down in the case of Kishan Gopal (supra)
are applicable to the facts of the present case".

entities.text: Meena Devi V/s Nunuchand Mahto and others, Special Leave Petition No.5345/2019
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the ocular statement of the mother of deceased, it is clear that deceased was a brilliant student and studying in a private school.

Therefore,
accepting the notional income earning Rs.30,000/ including future prospects and applying the multiplier of 15 in view of the decision of this court, in Sarla Verma (supra), the loss of dependency comes to Rs.4,50,000/ and if we (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 add Rs.50,000/ in conventional heads, then the total sum of compensation comes to Rs.5,00,000/.
17.
The ratio laid down in the above said citations are aptly applicable to the present case also.
The deceased girl had she been alive, would have certainly contributed substantially to the family of the petitioners by working hard.

It would be just and reasonable for to take her notional income of Rs.30,000/ and taking the young age of the parents namely the mother who was aged about 37 years old, at the time of accident, by applying legal principle, laid down in the case of Sarla Verma the multiplier applicable is 15.

Thus, Rs.30,000 x 15 = Rs.4,50,000/ Consequently the petitioners would be entitled for a sum of Rs.4,50,000/ towards loss of dependency and Rs.50,000/ under the conventional heads towards loss of love and affection, funeral expenses, last rites, and the said amount under the conventional heads is awarded even in relation to the death of children between 10 to 15 years old, the principles laid down in the case of Kishan Gopal and another V/s Lala and others in AIR 2014 SC (SUPP) 173 are applicable to the facts of the present case, wherein, the Apex Court had ruled that in the case of death of a minor in road (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 traffic accident, the claimants would be entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.5,00,000/.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and another V/s Lala and others in AIR 2014 SC (SUPP) 173
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the ocular statement of the father of deceased, it is clear that deceased was a brilliant student and studying in a private school.
Hence, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.50,000/ under conventional.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for fair, just and reasonable compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

18. The petitioners have relied upon following citations in support of their claim:
01. 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 330 in between Master Ayush V/s The Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., and another.

entities.text: Master Ayush V/s The Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But said citation is applicable to grievous injury case, but not to death case.

Yadukumar M vs Ravi Chandra on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9223321/
6 02. 2012 AIR SCW 6286 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Balakrishna and another.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Balakrishna and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein it is held that in package policy inmates of Car/vehicle covers the liability.
19. In this case the respondent No.1 was placed exparte and though the respondent No.3 has appeared through her counsel, but not contested the matter.
(SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 Though the respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement, but not lead any defence evidence.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement has taken contention that the respondent No.1 has no valid and effective driving licence and vehicle was registered for private vehicle and at the time of accident the vehicle was used for commercial purpose with excess seating capacity, thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

But Police have not filed Charge sheet against the driver, for driving the vehicle without driving licence and no evidence on record to show that the offending vehicle was used for commercial purpose.
It is also evident that the owner, driver and inmates of the car are all closed relatives and family members.
Hence, it cannot be said that the family members were hired the vehicle and it is used for commercial purpose.
Absolutely there is no evidence in this regard.
Further, the respondent No.2 admits that it has issued policy in favour of Nagesha.S who is the owner of the offending car.
Said Nagesha.S is also died in the said accident.

Further, as per insurance policy though it was not marked by either of the parties, but same was kept in records,
which indicates that it is motor private car package policy and is valid from 23.08.2021 to (SCCH3)
16 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 22.08.2022.
The alleged accident was occurred on 06.06.2022, it indicates that as on the date of accident the policy is valid and is in force.

Therefore, respondent No.1 being the driver, respondent No.2 being the insurer and respondent No.3 being the wife of the R.C. Owner of the offending car, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However,
as discussed above the insurance policy of the offending car is valid and is in force as on the date of accident, hence, the respondent No.2 being the insurer shall liable to pay above said compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.4:
In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

(SCCH3) 17 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 The petitioners are entitled for compensation of of Rs.5,00,000/ (Rupees Five lakhs only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 being the father and petitioner No.2 being mother of the deceased are entitled for Rs.2,00,000/ each in the award Yadukumar M vs Ravi Chandra on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9223321/
7 amount and the said award amount is not big amount, entire amount shall be released through E payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details.
On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.3 being the brother of the deceased is entitled for Rs.1,00,000/ in the award amount and the said award amount is not big amount, entire amount shall be released through E payment directly to his account by obtaining the bank account details.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
(SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.3802/2022 Draw award accordingly.

Hence, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.50,000/ under conventional.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has taken contention that the respondent No.1 has no valid and effective driving licence and vehicle was registered for private vehicle and at the time of accident the vehicle was used for commercial purpose with excess seating capacity, thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The alleged accident was occurred on 06.06.2022, it indicates that as on the date of accident the policy is valid and is in force.
Therefore, respondent No.1 being the driver, respondent No.2 being the insurer and respondent No.3 being the wife of the R.C. Owner of the offending car, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
